question: What is the primary purpose of a quality improvement team in nursing?

options.A: To conduct routine daily nursing shift handovers
options.B: To handle staff disciplinary hearings and queries
options.C: To manage hospital budgets and staff salaries
options.D: To address specific clinical or operational gaps

explanation: These teams specifically focus on analyzing workflows and fixing system problems to improve patient care outcomes. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why must frontline staff be included in quality improvement teams?

options.A: Hospital regulations strictly mandate their presence
options.B: They are responsible for purchasing hospital equipment
options.C: They have extra free time during shifts
options.D: They understand daily operational realities best

explanation: Frontline workers know where the actual bottlenecks occur because they experience them during routine patient care. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h1)

question: Who connects the quality improvement team to executive leadership and secures resources?
explanation: The sponsor acts as a bridge to upper management, helping to secure funding and administrative backing for the project. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h2)

question: What happens when a quality improvement team lacks clear divisions of labor?

options.B: Staff members complete the project much faster
options.C: Projects often stall due to neglected tasks
options.D: Team meetings become much shorter and focused

explanation: When nobody knows who is responsible for specific duties, essential steps like tracking metrics or running meetings get ignored. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is a major risk of building a team from only one professional group?

options.A: It creates a narrow siloed perspective
options.B: It makes meetings run much longer
options.D: It doubles the cost of the project

explanation: Single-discipline teams miss vital operational insights from other departments that interact with the same patient workflow. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h3)

question: A ward is launching a project to reduce patient falls. Who should be recruited alongside nurses?

options.A: Only medical laboratory scientists and receptionists
options.B: Physiotherapists, pharmacists, and estate management staff
options.C: Only senior nursing officers from the surgical unit

explanation: Physiotherapists manage mobility, pharmacists review fall-risk medications, and estate management addresses physical hazards like broken floor tiles. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h3)

question: What document acts as the operational contract for a quality improvement project?
explanation: The charter formally establishes the project scope, timeline, goals, and member responsibilities right at the start. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h4)

question: Why is a vague objective harmful to a quality improvement initiative?

options.A: It prevents nurses from administering medications
options.B: It immediately violates hospital labor laws
options.C: It stops the executive sponsor from paying staff
options.D: It leads to wandering discussions and wasted effort

explanation: Without a precise target, team members will pull the project in different directions without making real progress. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h4)

question: What term describes an environment where staff can speak up without fear of reprisal?
explanation: Psychological safety allows junior staff to highlight errors and suggest improvements without worrying about verbal abuse or victimization. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h5)

question: How should a team handle project setbacks during data reviews?

options.A: Analyze failures objectively rather than personalizing them
options.B: Hide the bad metrics from the executive sponsor
options.C: Blame the junior nurses for inaccurate data gathering
options.D: Immediately disband the team and start over

explanation: Treating setbacks as system flaws rather than personal failures keeps morale high and encourages honest problem-solving. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is a common reason why clinical staff resist new quality improvement protocols?

options.A: Fear of increased workload or unfamiliar workflows
options.B: A strict desire to work longer hours every day
options.C: Financial bonuses given for maintaining old routines
options.D: Mandatory government orders to reject changes

explanation: Staff worry that changes will disrupt their rhythm or add administrative burdens to an already heavy shift. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h6)

question: How should nursing leaders handle pushback from resistant colleagues?

options.A: Remove them permanently from the hospital ward
options.B: Listen actively and involve them in workflow redesign
options.C: Ignore their complaints until the project finishes
options.D: Issue immediate queries and threaten disciplinary action

explanation: Involving resistant staff helps address their genuine concerns and often turns them into advocates for the new process. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is required to sustain quality improvement gains over the long term?

options.A: Embedding new practices into standard operating procedures
options.B: Keeping the project team active with no end date
options.C: Stopping all data collection once targets are met
options.D: Disbanding the hospital management committee permanently

explanation: Formalizing changes into daily routines ensures the new habits persist even after the special project team concludes its work. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why are ongoing audit and feedback loops necessary after a project launches?

options.A: To fulfill legal requirements for patient admission
options.B: To justify cutting nursing salaries for poor metrics
options.C: To prove that the team leader deserves a promotion
options.D: To ensure staff compliance does not slip over time

explanation: Without continuous monitoring, clinical staff often slowly drift back into old, comfortable habits. [learn more](GST319_U2_T9#GST319_U2_T9_h7)
